name: Extra Space Storage Inc.
moat_justification: Largest U.S. self-storage operator by store count after the 2023 Life Storage merger, with density, a data/revenue-management platform across owned plus 1,964 third-party managed stores, and ancillaries (tenant reinsurance, bridge loans) — but the product is a commodity box on a month-to-month lease with near-zero switching costs, local fragmented competition, and demand hostage to housing turnover and new supply. Moderate/narrow moat: 5/10, CAP 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 14.3%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: High-quality self-storage REIT, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% on any scenario (weighted IRR 7.86%, weighted IV@15% $56.90 vs $133.96 price; hurdle-clearing price $56.90, even super-bull only $91.59).
moat_for: Largest U.S. operator by store count — local density lowers marketing cost per rental
Data / revenue-management platform across owned + 1,964 third-party managed stores
Ancillaries at scale: tenant reinsurance and bridge loans
moat_against: Commodity product, month-to-month leases, near-zero switching costs
Local fragmented competition — a new facility nearby erodes pricing directly
Demand hostage to housing turnover / mobility
New supply waves pressure rents and occupancy (94.2% in Q2 2026, flat YoY)
